Section 3  Nutrition in the Clinical Setting
development of cardiac cachexia. As myocardial function progressively deteriorates, 
patients present with loss of adipose tissue, bone mineral density, and loss of lean 
body mass. Deficiencies in both macro- and micronutrients contribute to the 
progression of the disease, but rarely initiate the wasting process.77,80,81 Upper-body 
and temporal wasting with lower-extremity edema are the hallmark features of this 
condition. New evidence suggests that patients with CHF also have alterations in 
intestinal morphology, permeability, and absorption function.77 This intestinal dys-
function may lead to both the chronic inflammatory state and catabolic/anabolic 
imbalance seen in cardiac cachexia. The proposed mechanisms to explain cardiac 
cachexia include:
●
